cz-1Tsw.title: House numbers: red with dividing line
cz-1Tsw.summary: Red house numbers with a dividing line and a Roman numeral are unique to Liberec. The line matters, as other cities have Roman numerals without it.

cz-2QUv.title: Landscape: rolling land, steep solitary hills
cz-2QUv.summary: In the north of Bohemia, rolling land with steep, lone hills, sometimes topped with castles.

cz-37rL.title: House numbers: yellow with black outline
cz-37rL.summary: Písek uses yellow house numbers with a black outline.

cz-47QH.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, five bigger stripes
cz-47QH.summary: Pedestrian crossing signs with five stripes.

differs.how: Slovak stripes are smaller, leaving more gap to the triangle edge

cz-7h9k.title: Google car: grey winter Gen 3, sometimes snow
cz-7h9k.summary: Much of the older Gen 3 coverage was taken in winter, so it looks very grey and sometimes snowy. Bulgaria and Hungary have this too, Slovakia mostly does not.

differs.how: Winter Gen 3 coverage is uncommon there

cz-7iZx.title: Houses: timber-framed, along northern border
cz-7iZx.summary: Timber-framed houses are mostly found along the northern part of the German border.

cz-7mO5.title: Houses: cube-shaped red brick functionalist
cz-7mO5.summary: Cube-shaped functionalist red brick houses in Zlín, built for shoe company workers, with similar high-rises downtown. Similar company towns exist in Slovakia and France.

cz-7uBV.title: Sign: red-white striped temporary posts
cz-7uBV.summary: Temporary square sign posts coated in red and white stripes are common here and in Slovakia.

cz-9iNw.title: Houses: colourful, well-kept prefab blocks
cz-9iNw.summary: Prefabricated panel apartment blocks are common in cities, as everywhere in the former Eastern bloc. Here they are well kept, often with bright colours and patterns. Slovakia is the same, Poland and Hungary a bit less.

cz-AJhg.title: Google car: white car
cz-AJhg.summary: A white Google car exists here but not in Slovakia. Other European countries can have a white car.

differs.how: Slovakia has no white Google car

cz-AWb6.title: Sign: black road number at bridge ends
cz-AWb6.summary: Black signs often stand at the end of bridges in Gen 4 coverage, with the road number on the left.

cz-AhNO.title: Sign: yellow bicycle route markers
cz-AhNO.summary: Bicycle signs are yellow. You may also see hiking-style markings with yellow stripes instead of white.

cz-CR8x.title: Sign: bright red street names
cz-CR8x.summary: The most common street sign is bright red, either wide on walls or thin on posts; similar blue ones are also common. The word for street is "ulice" (not "ulica"), though it is often left out.

differs.how: Slovakia typically uses white street signs

cz-Csne.title: Sign: blue or green highway signs
cz-Csne.summary: Blue or green highway signs with a thin white border, separated from the edge by a second coloured border.

differs.how: Slovak highway signs have the white border right on the edge

cz-E2r5.title: Windows: single-pane in the northwest
cz-E2r5.summary: Houses with single-pane windows are more common in the northwest.

cz-EtCV.title: House numbers: black and white pair
cz-EtCV.summary: A pair of black and white house numbers is found in Brno. The city district is written on the black one.

cz-GIEo.title: Sign: border set in from the edge
cz-GIEo.summary: The border of road signs is almost always separated from the edge by a strip in the sign's background colour.

differs.how: Slovak signs more often have the border on the edge

cz-GyNy.title: Streets: grey and white marble mosaic paving
cz-GyNy.summary: Downtown streets are often paved with grey and white marble stones, like in Portugal, often in square mosaic patterns. Similar paving appears in smaller amounts in other towns, so consider the city size.

cz-I7E1.title: Houses: thick dark wooden posts under upper
cz-I7E1.summary: Houses with thick, dark wooden posts holding up the upper floors are common in the far north.

cz-IPjG.title: Pole: short metal bars holding insulators
cz-IPjG.summary: Pole tops typically have short metal bars that hold the insulators. Same in Slovakia.

cz-IhlL.title: Google car: grey tape on antenna tip
cz-IhlL.summary: A grey piece of tape on top of the antenna, seen in much of the older Gen 3 coverage. Also in Slovakia, Hungary, Romania and Bulgaria.

cz-Ilr9.title: Sign: white street name with red text
cz-Ilr9.summary: White street signs with red text are most common in the east and also in the far south. Brno uses this design.

cz-JvWn.title: Sign: street names in two languages with Polish
cz-JvWn.summary: Bilingual Polish and local street signs in Český Těšín and very rarely nearby towns.

cz-KhBT.title: Bike paths: four digits increase clockwise
cz-KhBT.summary: Four-digit bike path numbers increase clockwise, starting in the south of Bohemia. They are not on Google Maps, so you have to remember the pattern. Paths starting with A belong to the capital.

cz-LOn9.title: Houses: suburban houses joined in pairs
cz-LOn9.summary: Suburban houses are commonly built connected in pairs, which is less common in neighbouring countries including Slovakia.

differs.how: Paired houses are less common there

cz-LS8m.title: Pole: concrete with trident top, arms angled up
cz-LS8m.summary: Concrete poles with a trident top, two arms angled upwards. The number of insulators varies but the shape stays the same. The rarest of these pole tops, and unique to this country and Slovakia.

cz-MXsC.title: Google car: red Gen 4
cz-MXsC.summary: A red newer-generation (Gen 4) car, found here and in Slovakia. Other European countries have red cars too.

cz-MkWo.title: Road numbers: first digit 1-6
cz-MkWo.summary: Road numbers start with 1 to 6, and those starting with 6 are scattered around the country. Roads 7, 8 and 9 all start in the capital and head north and northwest. Roads 1 to 5 follow the map, with some exceptions.

cz-NS13.title: Houses: folk baroque, richly decorated walls
cz-NS13.summary: Folk baroque (Selské Baroko) houses with highly decorated walls, in small villages around České Budějovice.

cz-NidB.title: House numbers: two octagons, inverted colours
cz-NidB.summary: Pilsen house numbers are two octagonal plates, red and white, with swapped colour schemes.

cz-PETs.title: Sign: thick black caps on sign posts
cz-PETs.summary: Sign posts typically have thick black caps. Some European countries have similar caps.

differs.how: Slovak posts usually have no caps

cz-PTbY.title: Pole: wide round concrete, often in pairs
cz-PTbY.summary: Wide, round concrete poles, quite often attached in pairs. Slovakia uses them too.

cz-QlQe.title: Phone numbers: 9 digits, 1-3 digit area code
cz-QlQe.summary: Numbers have 9 digits and the first 1-3 are the area code. If the first digit is 6 or higher it does not mark an area. They are not common.

cz-ShNI.title: Sign: hiking marker
cz-ShNI.summary: A hiking marker made of one coloured strip between two white ones, sometimes shaped like an arrow. Most common here and in Slovakia, but similar ones exist in Poland, Hungary and Germany.

differs.how: Similar markers are far rarer there

cz-THqa.title: Road lines: solid edge lines, no centre line
cz-THqa.summary: Often solid outer lines with no centre line. All neighbours have this, and Germany does too.

cz-U0oF.title: Language: acute accents, Ř Ě Ů
cz-U0oF.summary: A Slavic language with acute accents on vowels (á, é, í, ó, ú, ý). Ř, Ě and Ů are the Czech giveaways, while Slovak uses Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ and Ĺ. South Slavic languages have no vowel accents.

differs.how: Slovak uses Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ, Ĺ instead of Ř, Ě, Ů

cz-VqUC.title: Landscape: rolling hills, few tall mountains
cz-VqUC.summary: Fairly rolling land with many hills and height changes, but few tall mountains. Slovakia has more mountains and also more completely flat areas.

differs.how: More high mountains and more fully flat areas

cz-YKsZ.title: Bollard: orange double reflector front
cz-YKsZ.summary: A bollard with two orange reflectors on the front and one white reflector on the back. Rarer blue and red versions exist. Slovakia uses the same design.

cz-ZA6H.title: House numbers: blue or red with thin white
cz-ZA6H.summary: House numbers are on blue or red signs with thin white borders.

differs.how: Slovak numbers are on white signs with a thin red or black border

cz-b6fI.title: Sign: blue street names, more in the east
cz-b6fI.summary: Blue street signs can be found nearly everywhere but are more common in the east. Ostrava is the only major city that mainly uses them.

cz-bQbe.title: Road: km marker with yellow outline
cz-bQbe.summary: Kilometre markers have a yellow outline outside the black frame and no black horizontal line in the middle.

differs.how: Slovak markers have a black middle line and no yellow outline

cz-cQDy.title: Lamp post: thick base with paired bolts
cz-cQDy.summary: Lamp posts with a thick base fixed by pairs of bolts on opposite sides. The exact base shape varies. Also common in Slovakia.

cz-dfwx.title: House numbers: one red, one white, underlined
cz-dfwx.summary: In České Budějovice, house numbers are one red and one white plate with underlined numbers.

cz-hFSH.title: Google car: rare Gen 2 camera
cz-hFSH.summary: Rarely you can find coverage from the older Gen 2 camera (lower quality).

cz-k92w.title: Sign: arrow direction signs with filled tip
cz-k92w.summary: Arrow-shaped direction signs with a filled-in tip, recognisable even from behind.

cz-laf3.title: Sign: railway crossing with no background
cz-laf3.summary: Railway crossing signs have no background panel.

differs.how: Slovak crossing signs have a white rectangular background

cz-lm-740371.title: Sign: big red street name with fancy frame
cz-lm-740371.summary: Prague street signs are red, large, and have a distinctive ornate frame.

cz-lm-740374.title: Sign: red street name with city at the bottom
cz-lm-740374.summary: České Budějovice street signs are red with the city name written along the bottom.

cz-mhfL.title: Pole: striped gas or water poles beside the
cz-mhfL.summary: Striped gas and water poles that look like snow poles are often by the road. Many European countries have striped utility poles, so check the location and other clues.

cz-n1YQ.title: Wine: 95% comes from the eastern region
cz-n1YQ.summary: About 95% of wine comes from the eastern wine region of Moravia, so vineyards point east.

cz-nRTP.title: Houses: dark wood with white stripes
cz-nRTP.summary: Dark wooden houses with white stripes showing through the wood are common across most of the north.

cz-nepH.title: Sign: white street name with blue text
cz-nepH.summary: White street signs with blue text are most common in the east, and also appear in the central north.

cz-pe1N.title: Houses: long side to road, barn-sized doors
cz-pe1N.summary: In Moravia, town houses sit with their long side along the road, often joined in big groups, and have very large front doors like barn doors. Also common in northeastern Austria.

cz-qGBg.title: Google car: black Gen 4
cz-qGBg.summary: A black newer-generation (Gen 4) car, found here and in Slovakia. Many other European countries have one too.

cz-qmvg.title: Sign: white street name, blue text, red border
cz-qmvg.summary: A white street sign with blue text and a red border, the same as Slovakia's typical one, means you are near the Slovak border.

cz-r4zS.title: Pole: two braces under the bar
cz-r4zS.summary: Two support bars holding up the metal bar on the pole top, forming an upside-down triangle. Also seen in Slovakia, Germany, Albania, Serbia and Romania.

cz-t6TO.title: Chevron: white with red arrows
cz-t6TO.summary: White chevrons with red arrows, same in Slovakia. Less often red on yellow.

cz-tF8d.title: Sign: fairly thin font
cz-tF8d.summary: Road signs use a fairly thin font, the same as in Luxembourg and Germany.

differs.how: Slovak signs use a much bolder font

cz-xG48.title: Roof: diamond-shaped tiles
cz-xG48.summary: Roofs with diamond-shaped tiles are common here and in Slovakia, and somewhat common in Hungary.

cz-xfda.title: Guardrail: wider type B
cz-xfda.summary: A special type B guardrail that is wider than the normal one, used only here and in Slovakia. Czechia is very consistent, while Slovakia sometimes uses other types.

cz-xxAw.title: Sign: blue street name, text fills the sign
cz-xxAw.summary: In Šumperk, street signs are blue with text filling almost the whole sign.

cz-zEn7.title: Sign: white street name with black text
cz-zEn7.summary: White street signs with black text are most common in the southeast. They can look very similar to the blue-text ones.
